evidence.detail: R115 ScriptPacketDispatcher registers this exact class as ScriptPacket 5.
The handler reads selector, interface id and value, indexes the global R56 RSInterface table, and mutates only two integer fields on that exact widget.

Renderer/input code clamps RSInterface.V between 0 and RSInterface.aH - RSInterface.aR, uses V as the child-render vertical offset, and draws/updates the scrollbar when aH exceeds aR; this independently fixes V as scroll position and aH as scroll maximum/content height.
Selector 1 writes RSInterface.V; selector 2 writes RSInterface.aH. No other state is touched.

candidates.note: InterfaceScrollPacketHandler is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for ScriptPacket 5. The packet's complete target surface is proven as RSInterface scroll position/max state; confidence is 0.998.

evidence.detail: R115 ScriptPacketDispatcher registers this exact class as ScriptPacket 37.
The handler targets one R56 RSInterface and clears, sets one entry, fills, allocates, or removes its String[] ay array; RSInterface itself allocates ay to exactly the inventory-item array az length.
Inventory rendering reads ay[slot] for the current inventory slot and, when non-null, draws that String directly over the rendered item slot.

The packet's selector 4 writes the same RSInterface ac/ap pair decoded and used by inventory-style widget layout, so the same handler also controls the slot-grid spacing/layout paired with the per-slot overlay text.

candidates.note: InventorySlotOverlayPacketHandler is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for ScriptPacket 37. It controls per-slot inventory overlay Strings and their paired slot-grid layout state; confidence is 0.998.

evidence.detail: R115 ScriptPacketDispatcher registers this exact class as ScriptPacket 39.
The handler owns the sole static Trove int-to-int map. It reads item id plus integer value; value -2 removes the item key, otherwise the value is inserted/replaced.
The inventory renderer derives itemId as RSInterface.az[slot] - 1, checks this exact map for that item id, and draws the mapped integer as white text over the item slot.

A mapped value of -1 is rendered literally as '?', while other values are rendered through String.valueOf(int), fixing the payload as a numeric per-item overlay without asserting what the number semantically represents.

candidates.note: ItemNumericOverlayPacketHandler is deliberately narrower than guesses such as charges/value/count: exact v308 proves only a per-item numeric overlay map. Confidence is 0.998.
